featured_videos.title: Carnivore Wasn't Enough: How I Tanked!
featured_videos.creator: HomeSteadHow
featured_videos.editorial_title: Carnivore Wasn't Enough: How I Tanked!
featured_videos.commentary: You know what's wild? A bunch of people in the comments are basically saying the same thing: carnivore works, but it's not magic if your life is falling apart. Maggie's comment about keeping things simple during her family's grief hit different, and then you've got folks talking about stress, sleep, cortisol tanking their ketones even when they're doing everything "right." The thread really drives home that this isn't just about what's on your plate, it's about what's happening in your nervous system. If you've been frustrated thinking carnivore failed you, it might be worth looking at whether stress, trauma, or sleep deprivation are the real culprits. I actually touched on this in my piece about carnivore and mental health, but this video shows why tools like continuous ketone monitors can be genuinely useful, not for obsessing, but for understanding what your body's actually doing when life gets heavy.

featured_videos.title: No Seriously, Not All Carnivore Foods Are Safe (STOP EATING NOW)
featured_videos.creator: Professor Bart Kay - Nutrition and Health Science
featured_videos.editorial_title: No Seriously, Not All Carnivore Foods Are Safe (STOP EATING NOW)
featured_videos.commentary: Bart's hitting on something the community clearly feels viscerally about: it's not just about what you eat, it's about what's actually *in* it. The seed oil and margarine reaction tells you everything. People aren't being paranoid when they talk about inflammatory oils or processing methods that sneak toxins into foods that look "carnivore-friendly" on the surface. That canned fish point is worth sitting with too, because most of us assume if it's meat, it's safe. The real conversation here isn't carnivore vs. everything else, it's being intentional about sourcing and reading labels even when you're already doing the diet right.

featured_videos.title: ZERO CARB BREAD with 2 INGREDIENTS! Easy, No Flour, More Fiber and Protein, Cheap and Healthy (Keto)
featured_videos.creator: Patricia Delicious Nutrition
featured_videos.editorial_title: ZERO CARB BREAD with 2 INGREDIENTS! Easy, No Flour, More Fiber and Protein, Cheap and Healthy (Keto)
featured_videos.commentary: Look, the egg white situation is real. Multiple people hit the comments asking "How many eggs???" because 13 eggs for one loaf is a lot, even if you're all-in on low-carb cooking. That said, if you're already doing carnivore or keto, you probably have eggs for days. The flaxseed angle is interesting too, since some folks worry about fiber on a meat-based diet, though honestly the science here is different than worrying about plant fiber. What's getting me is that one comment about the texture. "Like eating Styrofoam" is brutal feedback, but it tells you this bread works better as a vehicle (chicken salad, butter, cinnamon) than as a standalone thing. That's actually helpful to know before you commit 13 eggs to an experiment.

featured_videos.title: EATING Too Much FAT On CARNIVORE Diet
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Tony Hampton - The Metabolic Health Doc
featured_videos.editorial_title: EATING Too Much FAT On CARNIVORE Diet
featured_videos.commentary: The comment section here is basically a masterclass in why one-size-fits-all diet advice fails. Some people are struggling to keep weight on eating 180g of butter daily, others hit a wall the moment they added too much dairy and fat, and a few are thriving on exactly that setup. Dr. Hampton's point lands because he's not saying fat is bad, he's saying your individual metabolic response matters more than the dogma. That one commenter who ditched the cheese and excess butter and jumped from stalled to 2lbs a week? That's the real story. It's also why tracking matters for people trying to troubleshoot, and if you're stuck, it might be worth checking what actually changed in your routine instead of assuming the diet itself stopped working.

featured_videos.title: Ex Carnivore: Why I'm NEVER Returning
featured_videos.creator: Vegetable Police
featured_videos.editorial_title: Ex Carnivore: Why I'm NEVER Returning
featured_videos.commentary: The comments section just answered the video for you. That top comment nailing "Kasey in 6 months" pretty much writes the script, and honestly, the guy saying "stop turning diet into ideology and figure out what works for YOU" is the most sane thing anyone said here. Look, people bounce off carnivore for real reasons sometimes, and that's fine, but the framing of "it's dead" and "never returning" followed by what looks like a search for attention tells you everything you need to know about where the real problem sits. Diet is a tool, not an identity. If carnivore isn't working for someone, they should eat differently, but the theatrical exit always reads the same way. What actually matters is whether you're getting results with your body, your energy, your health, no matter what diet that happens to be.

featured_videos.title: Someone You Know Is Eating Carnivore 😬
featured_videos.creator: Kent Carnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: Someone You Know Is Eating Carnivore 😬
featured_videos.commentary: Kent nails the core frustration in every comment here: people aren't actually skeptical about carnivore results, they're defensive about the narrative they've been sold. One person reversed heart disease and ditched T2DM medications entirely, another never gets sick anymore, and the community response is basically "yeah, and nobody wants to hear it because the system profits from keeping us confused." That farmer's point about profit motives driving nutrition guidelines isn't conspiracy thinking, it's just noticing that "eat the rainbow" and "five food groups" moved the needle on sales, not on actual health. If you've got someone in your life worried about your meat-only approach, this video's worth sharing because it reframes the real question: not whether carnivore works, but why admitting it works threatens so many people's sense of what they've been told is true.
